requirements.text: two of their installed products have mismatched warranty and entitlement periods ... you can reactivate expired entitlement
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE entitlement_id = 26 AND active = 1
assumptions: Acme is account 3 (Acme Systems); the two installed products are 15 (product 25, warranty_end 2029-07-07) and 17 (product 159, warranty_end 2027-10-16), the only ones whose product entitlements (26, 27) are inactive, both on the expired contract 133
entitlement 26 is product 25's only entitlement (contract 133, active = 0 on the seed); reactivating means active = 1

requirements.text: two of their installed products have mismatched warranty and entitlement periods ... you can reactivate expired entitlement
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE entitlement_id = 27 AND active = 1
assumptions: entitlement 27 is product 159's entitlement on contract 133 (active = 0 on the seed); its other two entitlements (16, 24) are active on live contracts
installed product 17 is retired on the seed, which the request does not mention and the policy does not bar for entitlement changes

requirements.text: they want everything aligned ... Update warranty contract end date if you have to
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contract WHERE contract_id = 133 AND status = 'active' AND end_date = '2029-07-07'
assumptions: 'warranty contract' read as the contract behind both entitlements, 133 (type support, status expired, end_date 2025-05-14 before its start 2025-08-27); Acme's warranty-type contract 7 is active and carries no entitlement for products 25 or 159

end_date 2029-07-07 is the later of the two installed products' warranty_end values (15: 2029-07-07, 17: 2027-10-16), the earliest single end that aligns one contract with both warranties; the original check agrees
status active follows from the policy: an entitlement is valid only when active and within an active contract's validity
no tool writes installed_product.warranty_end, so the alignment is made on the contract side

requirements.text: without interrupting any active cases tied to those products
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE account_id = 3 AND case_id IN (53, 57, 71) AND state IN ('new', 'in_progress', 'pending')
assumptions: the request forbids it: Acme's open cases on products 25 and 159 (53 on installed 17, new; 57 and 71 on installed 15, in_progress and new) must still be open afterwards; case 64 is closed and out of scope
not interrupted = still open; moving new to in_progress is allowed, resolving, closing or cancelling is not
disagreement: selector: A adds account_id = 3, B does not; same three rows on the seed; chose A's because it names the account the request is about

requirements.text: Update warranty contract end date if you have to
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM contract WHERE contract_id = 7 AND status = 'active' AND end_date = '2027-11-21'
assumptions: boundary of the 'warranty contract' selector: contract 7 is Acme's only warranty-type contract and a literal reading would extend it, but it carries none of the two products' entitlements, so it stays as it is

requirements.text: two of their installed products ... you can reactivate expired entitlement
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM entitlement WHERE entitlement_id = 25 AND active = 0
assumptions: boundary of the expired-entitlement selector: entitlement 25 is the account-wide (no product) inactive entitlement on the same contract 133; it belongs to no installed product, so the two-product request does not reach it

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on all six requirements (tables, anchors, cells, values) and on all three dispositions (kept). disagreement: case stay selector: A adds account_id = 3, B does not; same rows; kept A's (logged in the requirement). The request names neither the products, the entitlements nor the contract; all three are resolved from the seed (account 3's only inactive product entitlements, both on the one expired contract). The contract end date 2029-07-07 is the later warranty_end of the two installed products and the benchmark's value; a reviewer could argue for end_date >= '2029-07-07' instead of equality. Whether entitlement 25 (account-wide, same contract) must stay inactive is the judgement least supported by the request's words; both passes kept it as the boundary of the expired-entitlement selector. Installed product 17 is retired on the seed and the request does not ask to change it. Acting user 32 is an admin (active = 0 on the seed); the policy's default admin role is applied.
revised: the contract 133 requirement said warranty contract 7 outlives its products' warranties, but installed product 18 (product 170, covered by contract 7's entitlement 20) has warranty_end 2028-03-14, after contract 7's end 2027-11-21; the line now gives the reason that holds, that contract 7 carries no entitlement for products 25 or 159.
